title: When Delivering Bad News, Is It Better to Surprise Others or Give Them Advance Notice
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This Field Note weighs the tradeoffs between surprising someone with bad news versus giving advance notice. Surprise is shown to force quicker resolution and is common for terminations or urgent, unfolding events, but it also risks unpredictable and volatile emotional reactions. Advance notice allows people to prepare and process, generally producing more rational, constructive conversations and being perceived as more respectful -- though it can also breed unnecessary worry and is hard to deliver without effectively becoming the news itself. The piece ultimately recommends advance notice as the default when it's practically possible.
